This pioneering agreement marks the first step for municipalities to authorize the publication of their public spaces, such as parks and community centers, on Grafcan's cartographic viewer. The objective is to provide citizens with useful information for protection during extreme heat episodes, identifying safe and comfortable locations.
The Minister of Ecological Transition and Energy, Mariano H. Zapata, highlighted the initiative's importance within the climate change adaptation strategy. "It is essential to identify available refuges throughout the archipelago based on technical and homogeneous criteria," he stated, emphasizing that the tool will be useful for protecting the most vulnerable population.
The president of FECAM, María Concepción Brito, noted the Federation's commitment to this fight against climate change, calling the protocol "another step in applying public policies against an evidence we can no longer ignore." She thanked the Vice-Ministry for Ecological Transition for its impetus and called for funding to maintain and expand the network.
The Vice-Minister of Ecological Transition, Julieta Schallenberg, explained that the strategy aims to adapt urban spaces in the Canary Islands to rising temperatures, collaborating with municipalities, island councils, and the private sector. Municipalities are being supported with recommendation guides, and specific actions are being promoted, such as those carried out at the Piedra Hincada Sustainable Park (Guía de Isora) and projects in Los Realejos, San Bartolomé de Tirajana, Puerto de Tazacorte, and Santa Cruz de La Palma.
The Canary Climate Refuge Network is conceived as a constantly growing initiative, with over 1,000 field visits conducted and an estimated 250 potential refuges. Refuges are defined as urban spaces offering better temperature, humidity, and air quality conditions, especially for the elderly, children, and workers exposed to high temperatures.
Technical criteria establish requirements for indoor refuges (free access, drinking water, rest areas, restrooms, maximum temperature of 25°C) and outdoor ones (accessibility, shaded rest areas, vegetation cover over 75% for areas larger than 2,000 m²).

Rain is set to return to Andalucía this Thursday and Aemet (state meteorological agency) has issued yellow warnings for storms in three provinces.
The rain ... will start in the eastern part of the region from Wednesday afternoon, but Aemet has issued the yellow warnings for Thursday. They concern the provinces of Jaén, Granada and Almeria.
The weather warning will remain active from 2pm until midnight, due to accumulated rainfall of 15mm in one hour. This affects Cazorla, Segura, Guadix and Baza, as well as the Almanzora Valley and Los Vélez. ️
The forecast for Thursday predicts cloudy skies with medium and high clouds, with showers accompanied by thunderstorms in the eastern mountain ranges in the afternoon.
The rest of Andalucía expects no rain on Thursday. The weather will become more unsettled on Friday, with rainfall spreading across the whole of Andalucía.
According to the Aemet forecast, an Atlantic front is expected to bring cloudy or overcast skies across the entire mainland Spain this Wednesday, with warnings of rainfall on the Cantabrian coast of Navarre and in the Pyrenees.
Cloud cover will tend to decrease from north to south. Nevertheless, Aemet expects rainfall in the north-western half of the country, with significant accumulations in the eastern Cantabrian area and, to a lesser extent, in Galicia and the western part of the Central Mountain Range.
